title: In a CAM4 Green's function, DOISST mean steps change the 1982-2022 SST-pattern feedback by at most 0.17 W/m2/K; the AMIPII 2018 step and a post-2013 warm-pool data conflict change 2001-2022 by 0.3-0.8
abstract: Question: how much do known SST-product artifacts change the radiative feedback that the observed SST trend pattern implies, and which product differences are larger? Approach: we convolved monthly SST anomalies (fixed ice-free 60S-60N mask, 30,025 one-degree cells) with the CAM4 radiative-feedback Green's function (GF) of Dong et al. (2019) and computed lambda = trend(N)/trend(T). Records: published NOAA DOISST v2.1, OI SST v2 and the AMIPII forcing (PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.9), ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2, HadISST1, ESA SST CCI v3 trend maps, step-corrected DOISST (full and half correction), AMIPII without its 2018 step, and Roemmich-Gilson Argo (2005-2024). We used paired block-bootstrap intervals, exact step and regional attribution, a polar-fill variant and 39 West Pacific TAO/TRITON moorings. Results (W/m2/K): removing the DOISST mean steps changes the 1982-2022 feedback by -0.17 to -0.04 (mask) or +0.01 to +0.06 (polar fill), because their warm-pool and Southern Ocean effects cancel; published DOISST (-3.91) lies inside the reference range (-4.20 to -3.87). Removing the undocumented 2018 OI v2/AMIPII step changes the AMIPII feedback by +0.32 to +0.59 for 2001-2022 and +0.15 to +0.22 for 1982-2022; all intervals exclude zero. In 2001-2022 the products split by type: CCI, HadISST1 and DOISST give -3.5 to -3.6, ERSSTv5 and COBE-SST2 -3.0 and -2.8, and the DOISST corrections do not remove the split. The warm pool causes most of it. Moorings show that DOISST, OI v2 and HadISST1 warm faster than the buoys in the warm pool (+0.045 to +0.090 C per decade, 2001-2022), but Argo at the same sites also departs from the buoys by +0.105 C per decade after 2013 (0.0 in 2005-2013), when reporting moorings fell from about 27 to 6-11. Argo gives -3.44 for 2005-2022, near the satellite-type products; ERSSTv5 is less negative than Argo by +0.50 (2005-2024). Conclusion: the DOISST artifacts matter little for long-period GF feedback, but the AMIPII 2018 step and an unresolved post-2013 warm-pool disagreement between moorings and Argo each change CERES-era pattern feedbacks by several tenths of a W/m2/K. Limitations: one GF model; SST only within 60S-60N; corrections are fitted to imperfect references; moorings and Argo are partly product inputs; we cannot say which in situ system is correct.

display.caption: CAM4 Green's function feedback of the observed SST trend pattern by product: 1982-2022 and 2001-2022 on the fixed 60S-60N mask, and 2005-2022 on Argo-covered cells with Roemmich-Gilson Argo. Bars: 95% block-bootstrap intervals; squares: corrected versions (DOISST steps removed; AMIPII 2018 step removed); dashed: uniform warming.

Green's function feedback against the last year of the window for windows from 1982 (left) and 2001 (right). The AMIPII versions with and without the 2018 step separate after 2018; in 2001 windows, DOISST and HadISST1 stay much more negative than OI v2 and the in situ products.

Warm-pool checks at 39 TAO/TRITON sites: (a) product minus mooring trend 2001-2022; (b) 2005-2013 (open) and 2005-2022 (filled), with RG Argo; (c) annual differences relative to 2005-2013 and the number of reporting moorings. Argo and the moorings agree until 2013 and diverge after the array declined.
